expected_value: Sampling frame plus company identity and perhaps VAT/domain

decision: Use for sampling and entity resolution, not VAT discovery

evidence_observed: Accepts a supplied VAT number and returns status/name/address; it cannot search by company name
decision: Use only after discovery; manual checker for PoC and authenticated API at scale

expected_value: Public legal/footer pages might disclose VAT
evidence_observed: 10 eligible domains from 60 companies; 6 returned HTTP 200; 3 checksum-valid candidates; 2 HMRC-valid exact-entity matches
decision: Primary open-web source, but domain resolution and reachability are the main bottlenecks

expected_value: Search engines might directly surface VAT disclosures or public documents
evidence_observed: 20 deterministic attempts produced 7 identity leads, 4 relevant public-PDF appearances and 0 new attributable VAT candidates
decision: Useful for entity/domain research; poor primary VAT-discovery strategy in this sample

expected_value: Supplier questionnaires/contracts may expose company name and VAT together
evidence_observed: Contracts Finder contains public templates requesting registered VAT numbers, but many discovered documents contain placeholders or blank bidder fields
decision: Target completed award/contract documents only; templates do not count as VAT evidence

expected_value: An adjacent customs identifier may encode VAT
evidence_observed: Official HMRC guidance says the first 9 digits of a VAT-registered UK business's EORI equal its VAT number; non-VAT businesses may also have EORI
decision: Extract public EORI candidates and verify the first 9 digits through HMRC; never infer registration from EORI shape alone

expected_value: A legally required context should contain VAT
evidence_observed: Official HMRC guidance requires supplier name, address and VAT registration number on VAT invoices
decision: High-value source when invoices are lawfully available, but invoices are normally private and therefore not a general open-web acquisition channel
